question: How much is the insurance payout if I lose my thumb?
answer:
According to the policy, the payout for loss of a thumb is a percentage of the Sum Insured, depending on the severity:

- Loss of thumb – both phalanges: 25% of Sum Insured [p.13]
- Loss of thumb – one phalanx: 10% of Sum Insured [p.13]

Additionally, if the thumb is lost along with four fingers of one hand, the payout is 50% of Sum Insured [p.13].

question: Can I add my new spouse or baby to the policy and still get some benefits right away?
expected_answer: Yes, you can get continuity benefit for waiting periods already served, including the first 30 days, specific illness, and pre-existing disease waiting periods.
answer: Yes. You can add a newly married spouse (age up to 35) or newborn child (maximum 2 living children) within 120 days of marriage/birth [p.12]. Under the Plan Ahead benefit, the waiting periods already served by the policyholder are passed on to the newly added spouse or newborn, so they can get benefits right away for those conditions [p.12]. Also, a newborn baby is covered from day one up to 90 days of age, provided the mother is covered and the maternity claim is accepted [p.12].

question: What is considered when calculating associated medical expenses for my hospital treatment?
expected_answer: Associated medical expenses include nursing charges, operation theatre charges, and professional fees of medical practitioners, but do not include cost of pharmacy and consumables, cost of implants and medical devices, and cost of diagnostics, ICU charges.
answer:
Under the Star Health policy, associated medical expenses include nursing charges, operation theatre charges, and professional fees of the Medical Practitioner (Surgeon/Anaesthetist/Physician/Specialist). They exclude pharmacy and consumables, implants and medical devices, diagnostics, and ICU charges [p.7].

Under the SBI General policy, when a room rent limit is exceeded, associated medical expenses include room rent, nursing charges, Medical Practitioners' fees, and operation theatre charges, with proportionate deductions based on the room category. These deductions do not apply to ICU hospitalization [p.27].

question: Will my emergency transportation to the hospital be covered if I need to go to a different hospital for treatment?
expected_answer: Yes, if prescribed by a Medical Practitioner and is medically necessary, and the transportation is from one hospital to another that can provide the necessary medical services.
answer: Yes. Emergency transportation to another hospital is covered under the ambulance benefit if the transfer is from one hospital to another that is prepared to admit you and provide necessary medical services [p.6]. The transfer must be prescribed by a Medical Practitioner as medically necessary [p.6], and ambulance services from an existing hospital to another hospital are covered when advised by the treating Medical Practitioner in writing [p.4]. Another policy also covers private ambulance transport from one hospital to another for better medical treatment [p.11].

question: Will my insurance cover me if I get hurt while doing adventure sports like biking or rafting after drinking alcohol?

answer: No. Biking and rafting are listed as adventure sports [p.8], but the policy excludes payment for any adventure sports participation while under the influence of alcohol [p.8].

If the policy is ported with continuous prior coverage under IRDAI portability rules, the waiting period is reduced to the extent of prior coverage [p.31] [p.20].

question: What is considered an act of terrorism under my insurance policy?
expected_answer: An act or series of acts, including but not limited to the use of force or violence and/or the threat thereof, committed for political, religious, ideological or similar purposes.
answer: An act of terrorism is defined as an act or series of acts, including but not limited to the use of force or violence and/or the threat thereof, of any person or group(s) of persons, whether acting alone or on behalf of or in connection with any organization(s) or government(s), or unlawful associations, recognized under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (as amended from time to time) or any other related and applicable national or state legislation formulated to combat unlawful and terrorist activities in the nation for the time being in force, committed for political, religious, ideological or similar purposes including the intention to influence any government and/or to put the public or any section of the public in fear for such purposes [p.11][p.14]. An act of sabotage is defined as a subversive act or series of such acts committed for political, religious or ideological purposes including an intention to influence any [p.11][p.14].

question: Can I cancel my insurance at any time and if so, what happens to the money I've already paid?
expected_answer: You can cancel at any time and get a refund of the proportion premium for the unexpired policy period, if it's up to one year and you haven't made any claims.
answer:
Yes — you can cancel at any time. For the house policy, you can cancel by informing the insurer, and if the policy term is up to one year with no claims made, you get a proportionate refund of premium for the unexpired period [p.8] [p.15].

For the Star Health policy, the policyholder may cancel anytime by giving 7 days’ written notice. If the policy term is up to one year and there are no claims, the company refunds proportionate premium for the unexpired period. For policies longer than 1 year, premium is refunded for the unexpired period only for policy years where risk coverage has not commenced, after adjusting the long-term discount availed [p.40].

For the SBIGeneral Alpha health policy, the policyholder may cancel anytime by giving 7 days’ notice in writing. If the term is up to one year and there are no claims, proportionate premium for the unexpired policy period is refunded. For policies longer than 1 year, premium is refunded for the unexpired policy period only where risk coverage for those policy years has not commenced [p.28].

question: What law applies to how I name someone to get my policy money if something happens to me?
expected_answer: Section 39 of the Insurance Act, 1938
answer: For a life insurance policy, you can nominate a person to receive the policy money on your death, and you can change or cancel the nomination at any time before maturity; the change must be notified in writing to the insurer [p.7]. For a house insurance policy, you can nominate a person to receive the claim amount in the event of your death, either at policy inception or later, and you can change it at any time using the insurer's nomination form [p.10]. The house insurance policy is subject to the laws of India [p.10].
